title: ReNU SYNDROME
alt_titles: NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER WITH HYPOTONIA, BRAIN ANOMALIES, DISTINCTIVE FACIES, AND ABSENT LANGUAGE

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that ReNU syndrome (RENU) is caused by heterozygous mutation, typically arising de novo, in the RNU4-2 gene, which encodes the U4 small nuclear RNA, on chromosome 12q24.

checks.claim: ReNU syndrome (RENU) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the RNU4-2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we identify variants in RNU4-2, which encodes the U4 snRNA component of the major spliceosome, in an autosomal dominant disorder.
checks.explanation: Heterozygous variants in RNU4-2 are reported in 115 individuals with this NDD syndrome.

checks.claim: Heterozygous RNU4-2 mutations causing ReNU syndrome typically arise de novo.
checks.evidence_quote: Of the 47 rare allele instances in the regions, which we observed in 47 cases, 37 were determined to be de novo on the basis of genotype calls in the respective parents

checks.claim: The RNU4-2 gene encodes the U4 small nuclear RNA.
checks.evidence_quote: RNU4-2, which encodes U4 small nuclear RNA, a critical component of the spliceosome, was the most strongly associated gene.

checks.claim: The RNU4-2 gene is located on chromosome 12q24.
checks.evidence_quote: RNU4-2, which encodes U4 small nuclear RNA, a critical component of the spliceosome, was the most strongly associated gene.
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature added to the paper's gene.

paragraphs.text: ReNU syndrome is a neurodevelopmental disorder marked by global developmental delay, moderate to severe intellectual disability, hypotonia, and severely impaired or absent speech. Many patients also have seizures, microcephaly, short stature, distinctive facial features, and structural brain anomalies on imaging. The disorder is caused by de novo heterozygous mutations in a short, highly constrained region of the noncoding RNU4-2 gene, which encodes U4 snRNA, a component of the major spliceosome. It appears to be one of the most common monogenic causes of neurodevelopmental disorders.

checks.claim: ReNU syndrome is a neurodevelopmental disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Discovery and replication of RNU4-2 as an etiological gene for a novel neurodevelopmental disorder.

checks.claim: ReNU syndrome is marked by global developmental delay.
checks.evidence_quote: we find the RNU4-2 syndromic NDD to be characterized by moderate to severe global developmental delay
checks.explanation: GDD was present in 49 of 49 individuals.

checks.claim: ReNU syndrome is marked by moderate to severe intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: Moderate to severe/profound ID disproportionate to parental IQ unless the family history is consistent with an X-linked disorder
checks.explanation: ID is the main feature (91%), but 'moderate to severe' comes only from the enrollment criteria, not from a description of the cases' severity.

checks.claim: ReNU syndrome is marked by hypotonia.
checks.evidence_quote: ‘Generalized hypotonia’ in 39% (versus 13%, P = 8.08 × 10−4)
checks.explanation: Hypotonia is a feature of the syndrome.

checks.claim: ReNU syndrome is marked by severely impaired or absent speech.
checks.evidence_quote: Only three individuals (two with an SNV) had fluent speech, some had a few words and most were non-verbal.

checks.claim: Many patients with ReNU syndrome have seizures.
checks.evidence_quote: ‘Seizure’ in 52% (versus 27%, P = 3.13 × 10−2)

checks.claim: Many patients with ReNU syndrome have microcephaly.
checks.evidence_quote: ‘Microcephaly’ in 57% (versus 18% in other NDA-coded cases, Bonferroni-adjusted P = 3.23 × 10−7)

checks.claim: Many patients with ReNU syndrome have short stature.
checks.evidence_quote: ‘Proportionate short stature’ in 28% (versus 7%, P = 7.60 × 10−4)

checks.claim: Many patients with ReNU syndrome have distinctive facial features.
checks.evidence_quote: All but three were reported to have dysmorphic facial features.

checks.claim: Many patients with ReNU syndrome have structural brain anomalies on imaging.
checks.evidence_quote: Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed a spectrum of abnormalities in most individuals, most frequently reduced white matter volume, hypoplasia of the corpus callosum, ventriculomegaly, delayed myelination
checks.explanation: Abnormal brain MRI in 91% of individuals.

checks.claim: ReNU syndrome is caused by de novo heterozygous mutations in a short, highly constrained region of the RNU4-2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: forming two contiguous regions (n.62–70 and n.73–79) within which no unaffected participants had a rare variant. These regions were embedded within a genomic locus markedly depleted of variation in gnomAD
checks.explanation: The variants fall in short, constrained regions and are mostly de novo.

checks.claim: The RNU4-2 gene is noncoding.
checks.evidence_quote: compare rare variant genotypes in 41,132 noncoding genes
checks.explanation: RNU4-2 was identified in the noncoding gene analysis.

checks.claim: U4 snRNA, encoded by RNU4-2, is a component of the major spliceosome.
checks.evidence_quote: RNU4-2 is one of the genes encoding the U4 small nuclear RNA (snRNA) component of the small nuclear ribonuculeoprotein (snRNP) U4, which in turn is one of the five snRNPs of the major spliceosome.

checks.claim: ReNU syndrome appears to be one of the most common monogenic causes of neurodevelopmental disorders.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the U4 snRNA gene RNU4-2 cause one of the most prevalent monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders.

paragraphs.text: The name ReNU was proposed as an abbreviation built from RNU4-2 and neurodevelopmental disorder (Chen et al., 2024; Greene et al., 2024).

checks.claim: The name ReNU was proposed as an abbreviation built from RNU4-2 and neurodevelopmental disorder.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The name ReNU does not appear in the paper.

paragraphs.text: Chen et al. (2024) identified de novo variants in RNU4-2 in a large series of individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders, first in the Genomics England 100,000 Genomes Project and then in further cohorts. The patients had global developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, and severe speech impairment. Seizures, microcephaly, short stature, and brain imaging abnormalities were common, and the patients shared overlapping facial features.

checks.claim: Chen et al. (2024) identified de novo RNU4-2 variants in a large series of individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders.
checks.evidence_quote: In total, we identified 115 individuals with variants across this region, including 61 individuals in GEL (60 probands and one more sibling) and 54 from extra cohorts
checks.explanation: Mostly de novo variants in a large series.

checks.claim: Chen et al. (2024) first identified de novo RNU4-2 variants in the Genomics England 100,000 Genomes Project and then in further cohorts.
checks.evidence_quote: We searched for variants across this region in GEL, and also in further cohorts containing undiagnosed individuals with NDD (Methods).
checks.explanation: The variant was first identified in GEL, and the search was then extended to other cohorts.

checks.claim: Patients with de novo RNU4-2 variants reported by Chen et al. (2024) had global developmental delay.
checks.evidence_quote: Neurodevelopmental | GDD | 49 out of 49 | 100

checks.claim: Patients with de novo RNU4-2 variants reported by Chen et al. (2024) had intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: ID | 45 out of 45 | 100

checks.claim: Patients with de novo RNU4-2 variants reported by Chen et al. (2024) had hypotonia.
checks.evidence_quote: Hypotonia | 39 out of 45 | 87

checks.claim: Patients with de novo RNU4-2 variants reported by Chen et al. (2024) had severe speech impairment.
checks.evidence_quote: Speech abnormality | 45 out of 48 | 94 - non-verbal | 35 out of 45 |

checks.claim: Seizures were common among patients with de novo RNU4-2 variants reported by Chen et al. (2024).
checks.evidence_quote: Seizures | 37 out of 48 | 77

checks.claim: Microcephaly was common among patients with de novo RNU4-2 variants reported by Chen et al. (2024).
checks.evidence_quote: Microcephaly | 37 out of 48 | 77

checks.claim: Short stature was common among patients with de novo RNU4-2 variants reported by Chen et al. (2024).
checks.evidence_quote: Short stature | 37 out of 49 | 76

checks.claim: Brain imaging abnormalities were common among patients with de novo RNU4-2 variants reported by Chen et al. (2024).
checks.evidence_quote: Abnormal brain MRI | 41 out of 45 | 91

checks.claim: Patients with de novo RNU4-2 variants reported by Chen et al. (2024) shared overlapping facial features.
checks.evidence_quote: These facial features varied but consisted of a myopathic face with deep set eyes (some widely spaced and some narrowly spaced), epicanthus, wide nasal bridge
checks.explanation: The paper describes recurring facial features.

paragraphs.text: Greene et al. (2024) independently found RNU4-2 variants in patients with neurodevelopmental disorders in the 100,000 Genomes Project and described a similar phenotype. They concluded that the disorder is among the most common monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders.

checks.claim: Greene et al. (2024) independently found RNU4-2 variants in patients with neurodevelopmental disorders in the 100,000 Genomes Project.
checks.evidence_quote: we conducted a genetic association analysis using whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data on 77,539 participants enrolled in the 100,000 Genomes Project (100KGP).
checks.explanation: Variants were found in 100KGP cases with neurodevelopmental disorders.

checks.claim: Greene et al. (2024) described a phenotype in patients with RNU4-2 variants similar to that reported by Chen et al. (2024).
checks.evidence_quote: a syndrome characterized by ID, microcephaly, short stature, hypotonia, seizures and motor delay
checks.explanation: The phenotype is described, but the paper does not compare it with Chen et al.

checks.claim: Greene et al. (2024) concluded that the RNU4-2-related disorder is among the most common monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the U4 snRNA gene RNU4-2 cause one of the most prevalent monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders.

paragraphs.text: The heterozygous RNU4-2 mutations in ReNU syndrome occurred de novo in the patients reported by Chen et al. (2024) and Greene et al. (2024).

checks.claim: The heterozygous RNU4-2 mutations in patients with ReNU syndrome reported by Chen et al. (2024) occurred de novo.
checks.evidence_quote: In one individual the n.65A>G variant appeared to be mosaic in the mother (54 reference and eight alternate reads) and in another an SNV was maternally inherited (n.76C>T).
checks.explanation: Most variants were de novo (86 of 115 confirmed), but one SNV was inherited from the mother and in one case the mother appeared mosaic, so not every variant arose de novo.

checks.claim: The heterozygous RNU4-2 mutations in patients with ReNU syndrome reported by Greene et al. (2024) occurred de novo.
checks.evidence_quote: In total, 19 of the 26 affected probands acquired the variant de novo, six acquired the variant with inheritance that was unknown because of a lack of parental genotype data and one case inherited variant n.76C>T from an affected mother.
checks.explanation: Most variants were de novo, but some had unknown inheritance and one was inherited from an affected mother.

paragraphs.text: Chen et al. (2024) used whole-genome sequencing in patients with neurodevelopmental disorders and found an excess of de novo variants in RNU4-2. The variants clustered in a short critical region of about 18 nucleotides. This region includes the stem III region and the adjacent T-loop, which are involved in U4-U6 pairing and in positioning the 5-prime splice site in the spliceosome. The most frequent variant was a single-nucleotide insertion, n.64_65insT. The variants were absent from population databases. RNA sequencing of patient blood samples showed changes in 5-prime splice site usage. Earlier studies had missed this gene because RNU4-2 is a small noncoding gene that exome capture kits cover poorly.

checks.claim: Chen et al. (2024) used whole-genome sequencing in patients with neurodevelopmental disorders.
checks.evidence_quote: Using a cohort of 8,841 probands with genetically undiagnosed NDD in the Genomics England 100,000 genomes project (GEL)

checks.claim: Chen et al. (2024) found an excess of de novo variants in RNU4-2 in patients with neurodevelopmental disorders.
checks.evidence_quote: This includes 60 out of 8,841, or 0.68%, of all genetically undiagnosed NDD probands in GEL. By contrast, variants in this region are observed in 39 out of 490,132 (0.008%) individuals in the UK Biobank (OR = 85.8
checks.explanation: Shows the excess of variants in NDD probands.

checks.claim: The de novo RNU4-2 variants identified by Chen et al. (2024) clustered in a short critical region of about 18 nucleotides.
checks.evidence_quote: we identify variants in a critical 18 base pair (bp) region in the centre of RNU4-2

checks.claim: The RNU4-2 critical region includes the stem III region and the adjacent T-loop.
checks.evidence_quote: We identify an 18 base pair region of RNU4-2 mapping to two structural elements in the U4/U6 snRNA duplex (the T-loop and stem III)

checks.claim: The stem III region and T-loop of U4 snRNA are involved in U4-U6 pairing and in positioning the 5-prime splice site in the spliceosome.
checks.evidence_quote: Both regions are thought to stabilize U4/U6 pairing and accurately position the U6 ACAGAGA sequence to receive the 5′ splice site during initial spliceosome assembly

checks.claim: The most frequent RNU4-2 variant identified by Chen et al. (2024) was a single-nucleotide insertion, n.64_65insT.
checks.evidence_quote: Most individuals (77.4%) have the same highly recurrent single base insertion (n.64_65insT).

checks.claim: The RNU4-2 variants identified by Chen et al. (2024) were absent from population databases.
checks.evidence_quote: It is seen in a single individual in the UK Biobank (allele frequency of 1.02 × 10−6) with a variant allele balance consistent with a true variant
checks.explanation: n.64_65insT occurs in one UK Biobank individual, and variants in the critical region occur in 39 of 490,132 UK Biobank individuals. The variants are not absent from population databases.

checks.claim: RNA sequencing of blood samples from patients with RNU4-2 variants showed changes in 5-prime splice site usage.
checks.evidence_quote: Using RNA sequencing, we show how 5' splice-site use is systematically disrupted in individuals with RNU4-2 variants
checks.explanation: The RNA-seq was done on blood samples.

checks.claim: Earlier studies had missed RNU4-2 because it is a small noncoding gene that is poorly covered by exome capture kits.
checks.evidence_quote: This region, despite being within a highly conserved non-coding exon, is not included in commercially available clinical exome sequencing capture, which primarily targets protein-coding exons.
checks.explanation: The paper confirms exome capture does not cover the region and that detection by exome is poor. It does not say outright that earlier studies missed the gene for this reason, or that its small size was a factor.

paragraphs.text: Greene et al. (2024) independently identified de novo variants in the same region of RNU4-2 in patients from the 100,000 Genomes Project. The recurrent n.64_65insT variant was the most common.

checks.claim: Greene et al. (2024) independently identified de novo variants in the same critical region of RNU4-2 in patients from the 100,000 Genomes Project.
checks.evidence_quote: We implicated de novo variants among 47 cases in two regions of RNU4-2 in the etiology of a syndrome
checks.explanation: De novo variants in specific regions are reported, but the paper does not compare them with another study's region or describe the finding as independent.

checks.claim: The recurrent RNU4-2 n.64_65insT variant was the most common variant identified by Greene et al. (2024).
checks.evidence_quote: The most common variant, n.64_65insT, was observed as a de novo mutation in 33 different families.

paragraphs.text: Chen et al. (2024) proposed that variants in the critical region of U4 snRNA disrupt how the U4/U6 di-snRNP interacts with the 5-prime splice site during spliceosome assembly. This would alter 5-prime splice site selection, consistent with the splicing changes they observed in patient samples.

checks.claim: Chen et al. (2024) proposed that variants in the critical region of U4 snRNA disrupt how the U4/U6 di-snRNP interacts with the 5-prime splice site during spliceosome assembly.
checks.evidence_quote: insertion of a single base into the T-loop or stem III regions may destabilize the U4/U6 interaction and/or alter the positioning of the U6 ACAGAGA sequence and potentially disrupt the correct loading of the 5′ splice site into the fully assembled spliceosome
checks.explanation: The gist matches, but the paper frames the proposal mainly around insertions and talks about the U4/U6 interaction or duplex, not the 'U4/U6 di-snRNP'.

checks.claim: Chen et al. (2024) proposed that variants in the U4 snRNA critical region would alter 5-prime splice site selection, consistent with the splicing changes observed in patient samples.
checks.evidence_quote: This proposed effect is supported by the observed systematic disruption to 5′ splice-site use observed in RNA-seq data from five individuals with RNU4-2 variants.

paragraphs.text: In many unrelated patients with ReNU syndrome, Chen et al. (2024) and Greene et al. (2024) identified a de novo heterozygous 1-bp insertion (n.64_65insT) in the RNU4-2 gene. It was the most frequent variant in the critical region of the gene.

checks.claim: A de novo heterozygous 1-bp insertion (n.64_65insT) in the RNU4-2 gene was identified in many unrelated patients with ReNU syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: The most common variant, n.64_65insT, was observed as a de novo mutation in 33 different families.

checks.claim: The RNU4-2 n.64_65insT variant was the most frequent variant in the critical region of RNU4-2.
checks.evidence_quote: The most common variant, n.64_65insT, was observed as a de novo mutation in 33 different families.
checks.explanation: It was the most common variant in the regions.
